notes: The session's web search allowance was already used up when this part began (every search was refused), so nothing was searched. Everything was found by reading known addresses directly with the kit's honest User-Agent (states/net.py, patient lookups, robots.txt checked first for each site): the campaign websites the candidates filed with the Secretary of State (already in sl_websites; read-only), each government's own site reached from its home page, dfl.org/endorsed, mngop.com, and four Wikipedia election pages. Candidates with no entry are the ones this left out of reach.

Mark Koran (markkoranmn.com) and Todd Buchwald (toddformn.com): the filed campaign sites answered with a CAPTCHA page (/.well-known/sgcaptcha/). It was not worked around or asked again, so no website is recorded here for either; the filed address stays as filed.
Yellow Medicine County's site (co.ym.mn.gov) asks scripts to stay out in robots.txt, so nothing was read there and Mark Gruenes has no findings.
The Minnesota Judicial Branch and Governor's sites were not asked (earlier parts report a 403 and a CAPTCHA), so Carrie Ryan Gallia has no findings.

No findings, names not on the government's own page of sitting members or not reachable without a search: _ Rocco (Senate District 65; not on dfl.org, mngop.com's nominees page or Wikipedia's 2026 Senate page), John Hintz (not on Norman County's board page), TJ Lynch beyond his website, Jeffrey Sheridan, Mark Borland (not on Hibbing's council page), Dan Stone (not on Champlin's council page), Amy Reynertson, Virgil Aguirre Jr, Josh Perkerewicz (not on their districts' board pages).
TJ Lynch's campaign site says he served as Chief of Police in Lyle and is Captain of the Mower County Sheriff's Office; these are jobs without years, so they are not recorded as offices.

Samantha Wolf: the own_words quote is a line on her own Endorsements page; a letter of support is not a party endorsement and no party page for it could be reached (sd47dfl.org has no address), so there is no endorsed_by.
Some government pages print members' contact details next to their names; none was kept, and the reader blanked phone numbers and e-mail addresses before printing.
